No canyons or gorge streams in the flat Chicago region; nearest canyoning is in the Rockies/Utah (about 3 h flight).
No flooded caves in the Chicago area; nearest cave diving is Florida springs (about 3 h flight).
No natural caves in the Chicago region (glacial till over bedrock); nearest show caves are in southern Wisconsin or Illinois (about 3-5 h drive).
No glaciers in the Midwest; the nearest glacier trekking is in Glacier National Park, Montana, or the Canadian Rockies, a 3-4 hour flight away.
Go Ape treetop adventure with more than 40 rope obstacles, swings and ziplines across five sections; coverage is from its 2016 opening.
Vertical wind tunnel flights for first-timers at iFLY Chicago Rosemont near O'Hare, simulating freefall.
No artificial luge track in the Chicago area; nearest is Utah Olympic Park near Park City, Utah (about 3.5 h flight) or Lake Placid, New York (about 2 h flight plus a drive).
Chicago is flat glacial plain with no mountains; nearest real mountaineering is the Rockies near Denver (about 2.5 h flight).
Open-air tandem skydives at drop zones such as Skydive Chicago in Ottawa, about 1 hour 15 minutes by road; the metro area itself has only an indoor wind tunnel.
Tandem paragliding and paramotor courses from a site in Cullom, about 90 minutes southwest; the Indiana Dunes are a local free-flying site.
No free-roaming African wildlife around Chicago; Brookfield Zoo (about 22 km west) has African savanna exhibits with lions, and real safaris are in Africa.

No desert or dune field suitable for sandboarding near Chicago; the nearest established sandboarding is at Great Sand Dunes National Park in Colorado, well over 1,500 km away (equipment rentals at Alamosa).
Carpet-turf indoor ski school with classes and open gyms, plus a simulator-and-treadmill ski training studio in Schaumburg.

Villa Olivia in Bartlett (about 45 km west) runs small snow-made slopes for skiing with group, private and kids lessons in winter; Wilmot Mountain in Wisconsin (190 ft vertical, about 85 km north) is the nearest larger hill.
No volcanoes in the region; volcano boarding is done on Cerro Negro in Nicaragua, a roughly 5-hour flight away.
Class 1-2 rafting (rain and water-level dependent) on the Vermilion River from Lowell to Oglesby, about 90 miles southwest near Starved Rock.
Go Ape treetop course in the Cook County forest preserves with five sections and ziplines up to 600 ft; coverage is from its 2016 opening.
